# ts-parity fixtures

Golden-output JSON dumped from the TypeScript graph engine in
`civ-pro-the-gathering` (`src/lib/graph/*.ts` + `src/lib/statechart.ts`), one
file per statechart pack in `civ-pro-the-gathering/content/statecharts/*.json`.
Used to parity-test the `litgraph` Rust port against the original TS
implementation, node-for-node and edge-for-edge.

Generated by a dump script run with `pnpm exec tsx` against the TS source
directly (no build step, no modification to civ-pro-the-gathering). Object
keys are sorted recursively (`sortKeysDeep`) so diffs against a
re-generated fixture, or against the Rust port's own JSON dump, are stable.
All numbers are written at full JS `double` precision (no rounding).

Regenerate: `pnpm exec tsx <path-to-dump.ts>` from the civ-pro-the-gathering
repo root. The dump script itself lives outside this repo (a throwaway
scratchpad script, not checked in here or there); ask if you need to
re-run it and don't have it handy — it's a straightforward ~250-line driver
over the exports of `src/lib/graph/index.ts` and `src/lib/statechart.ts`.

## `v1-packs/`

Frozen copies of `packs/<id>.json` **as of schema v1** (byte-for-byte, taken
before the v2 migration that authored payoffs/hours/durations/roles/sources
onto these six packs). `crates/litgraph/tests/parity.rs` loads the pack from
here, not from the live `packs/` directory, because the golden output above
is only valid against the exact content that produced it: an authored
`payoff` (replacing the heuristic), authored `hours` (replacing an absent
field the TS engine treated as 0), or an authored `duration` all legitimately
change what the engine computes. Parity is a claim about the *engine*
reproducing the TS implementation, not about `packs/` staying frozen forever
— so the pack content parity needs is pinned here, independent of `packs/`'s
own evolution. If `packs/` ever needs a *structural* change (nodes/edges
added or removed, ids renamed) that should also flow into what parity checks,
update both copies deliberately; a content-only authoring change (payoffs,
hours, durations, roles, sources) should touch only `packs/`.

## Files

One `<pack-id>.json` per pack, e.g. `mpep-prosecution.json` for
`content/statecharts/mpep-prosecution.json`. `<pack-id>` is the JSON
filename stem, which also equals `chart.id` for every pack in this repo.

## Parameters used (all packs, all sections)

- `rate = 500` ($/attorney-hour) — the primary rate for every section below
  except where noted.
- `rateLow = 250` — a second rate, valueIteration only (see below).
- `policyDiffRateA = 150`, `policyDiffRateB = 1500` — the two rates
  `policyDiff` is diffed between.
- Pareto frontier: default options (`maxNodeVisits: 1` i.e. loopless/simple
  paths, `maxPaths: 50000`), **unless** a single terminal's `paretoPaths`
  call took longer than `paretoSlowThresholdMs = 20000` wall-clock ms, in
  which case it was re-run with `{ maxPaths: 20000 }` and that override is
  recorded per-terminal in `paretoPaths500.<terminal>.optionsUsed`. In this
  run, **no terminal on any pack exceeded 20s** (worst case was
  `frcp-civil-procedure` / `judgment-reversed-remanded` at ~6.9s), so every
  `optionsUsed` is `{}` (defaults) — `truncated: true` on some terminals
  still occurs where the *default* 50000-path cap itself was hit; that is
  normal DFS enumeration truncation, not the slow-path override.
- All other sections (weightedGraph, dijkstra, absorbingChain, SCC,
  dominators, minCut, policyDiff) use only `rate = 500` — there is a single
  authoritative dollar-cost model per fixture file for those sections.

Every top-level `params` object in each fixture file also records these
values inline (do not rely on this README alone).

## Top-level shape

```jsonc
{
  "packId": "mpep-prosecution",
  "packTitle": "...",                 // chart.title
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "startNodeId": "pre-filing",        // chart.startNodeId
  "terminals": ["...", ...],          // sorted node ids where kind === "terminal"
  "params": { ... },                  // see above
  "valueIteration500": { ... },
  "valueIteration250": { ... },
  "weightedGraph500": { ... },
  "dijkstra500": { ... },
  "absorbingChain500": { ... },
  "scc": { ... },
  "dominators": { ... },
  "minCut500": { ... },
  "paretoPaths500": { ... },
  "policyDiff_150_1500": { ... }
}
```

### `valueIteration500` / `valueIteration250`

Output of `valueIteration(chart, rate)` with default options
(`epsilon: 1e-6`, `maxIterations: 1000`), plus a derived per-edge view:

- `converged: boolean`, `iterations: number`
- `value`: `{ [nodeId]: number }` — V*(s), sorted by nodeId.
- `policy`: `{ [nodeId]: {from, to, label} }` — the applicant's optimal
  outgoing edge at each player/mixed node (absent at stochastic/terminal
  nodes), sorted by nodeId.
- `qValue`: `{ [key]: number }` — **as returned by the TS engine, unmodified**.
  Key is `"${from}→${to}"` (a literal `→`, U+2192). **This collides on
  parallel edges** (two edges with the same `from`/`to` but different
  `label`) — the TS `Map`'s last-write-wins semantics decide which
  survives, in `chart.nodes` iteration order. Do not treat this field as
  authoritative for packs with parallel edges; use `edgeQ` instead.
- `qValueNote`: human-readable restatement of the above collision caveat,
  embedded in the fixture itself so it survives even if this README drifts.
- `edgeQ`: `[{from, to, label, q}]` — **collision-free**. One entry per
  `chart.edges` element (including parallel edges), computed directly from
  the final converged value map as `q = -dollarCost(edge, rate) + V(edge.to)`,
  where `dollarCost` includes the same fee-shift adjustment
  `buildWeightedGraph` applies (i.e. `wg.edges[i].weight.dollarCost`, not
  the profile-unaware `edgeDollarCost()` helper). Sorted by
  `(from, to, label)`. This is the field the Rust port should diff against
  edge-for-edge.

### `weightedGraph500`

Output of `buildWeightedGraph(chart, 500)`:

- `edges`: `[{from, to, label, dollarCost, days, hours, fees, probability, benefit}]`,
  sorted by `(from, to, label)`. `probability` is `null` (not `undefined`)
  when the edge carries none (applicant edges, or a world edge on a node
  that isn't fully probability-authored). Note `dollarCost` already
  reflects the fee-shift discount when applicable — it is NOT simply
  `hours * rate + fees`; see `weights.ts`'s `buildWeightedGraph` for the
  fee-shift-eligibility rule (a structural reverse-reachability proxy, not
  a true conditional-probability calculation — documented as a known
  simplification in the TS source).
- `terminalValue`: `{ [nodeId]: number }` — 0 for non-terminals, sorted.

### `dijkstra500`

Three independent shortest-path runs from `chart.startNodeId` to **every**
terminal (not just one), each `{ [terminal]: PathResult | null }`:

- `cheapestByDollars` — weight = `wg.edges[i].weight.dollarCost` (i.e. the
  fee-shift-adjusted cost from `buildWeightedGraph`, matched by object
  identity back to `wg.edges`) — this is `cheapestPathByDollars`'s
  underlying weight function reproduced directly against `wg`, not the
  library's `edgeDollarCost(e, rate)` helper (those agree only when no edge
  on the shortest path is fee-shift-eligible).
- `fastestByDays` — weight = `edge.deadline?.length ?? 0`.
- `leastHours` — weight = `edge.hours ?? 0`.

`PathResult` is `{ target, nodes, total }` where `nodes` is the ordered
node-id path from start to target inclusive, and `total` is the summed
weight. `null` when the terminal is unreachable from the start node under
that weight function (Dijkstra only ever returns null for true
unreachability — all weights here are non-negative).

### `absorbingChain500`

Output of `absorbingChainAnalysis(chart, 500)` under its **default policy**
(best applicant edge per node, ranked by `valueIteration`'s Q*). Two shapes:

- Success: `{ ok: true, dataQuality: "exact"|"partial", absorptionProbabilityAtStart, expectedCostAtStart, expectedDaysAtStart, expectedStepsAtStart, policy }`,
  where the four `*AtStart` fields are that stat's value specifically at
  `chart.startNodeId` (the full per-transient-state maps are large and
  start-node values are what parity tests need; `absorptionProbabilityAtStart`
  is `{ [terminalId]: number }`, sorted, omitting zero-probability terminals
  per the TS engine's own `1e-9` cutoff). `policy` is `{ [nodeId]: {from,to,label} }`,
  sorted.
- Failure (singular transition matrix — the resolved policy induces a
  closed non-absorbing cycle, e.g. a self-loop the default policy can't
  escape): `{ ok: false, error: "<exact thrown message>" }`. **This
  happens for `frcp-civil-procedure` in this fixture set** — see below.

### `scc`

Output of `computeSCC(chart)`, with all node-id arrays sorted (the TS
return type does NOT sort component membership — Tarjan's algorithm order
is an implementation detail — so this fixture normalizes it):

- `components`: every SCC, each a sorted array of node ids.
- `componentOf`: `{ [nodeId]: componentIndex }` — **the index is
  positional into the TS engine's own unsorted `components` array** (Tarjan
  discovery order), NOT an index into this fixture's sorted `components`
  array. If the Rust port produces components in a different order, compare
  component *membership* (as sets), not these integer indices.
- `absorbingComponents`, `cyclicComponents`: subsets of `components`
  (same sorting), filtered per the TS engine's definitions (absorbing = no
  outgoing condensation edges; cyclic = size > 1, or a single node with a
  self-loop).
- `condensation`: `{ nodes: number[], edges: [{from, to}] }` over the same
  `componentOf` indices as above, deduped, sorted by `(from, to)`.
- `cyclicLoops`: one entry per `cyclicComponents` element, in the same
  order, each `{ nodes, internalEdges, escapeEdges }` (edges as
  `{from,to,label}`, sorted).

### `dominators`

Output of `computeDominators(chart)` (default root = `chart.startNodeId`):

- `root`: the root node id.
- `idom`: `{ [nodeId]: immediateDominatorNodeId }`, sorted — **only nodes
  reachable from `root` are present** (unreachable nodes are omitted by the
  TS engine, not defaulted to anything). The root maps to itself.

### `minCut500`

`minCut(chart, chart.startNodeId, terminal)` for **every** terminal:
`{ [terminal]: { value: number, cutEdges: [{from,to,label}] } }`, cutEdges
sorted by `(from, to, label)`. `value` is the max-flow/min-cut size (unit
capacities — i.e. the number of edge-disjoint start→terminal paths).

### `paretoPaths500`

`paretoPaths(chart, chart.startNodeId, terminal, 500)` for **every**
terminal: `{ [terminal]: { frontier, enumeratedCount, truncated, optionsUsed } }`.

- `frontier`: `[{totalDays, totalCost, nodes}]`, sorted by
  `(totalDays, totalCost)`. Non-dominated (days×dollars) paths only.
- `enumeratedCount`: total paths DFS'd before filtering to the frontier.
- `truncated`: true if the `maxPaths` cap (50000 by default, or 20000 if
  the slow-path override kicked in — see `optionsUsed`) was hit.
- `optionsUsed`: `{}` if default options were used (true for every
  terminal in this fixture set), or `{ maxPaths: 20000 }` if the >20s
  slow-path override applied (see Parameters above — did not trigger for
  any pack/terminal in this run).

### `policyDiff_150_1500`

`policyDiff(chart, 150, 1500)`:

- `rateA: 150`, `rateB: 1500`.
- `flips`: `[{nodeId, edgeA, edgeB}]`, sorted by `nodeId` — every node
  where the optimal policy edge differs between the two rates (edgeA = the
  optimal edge at rate 150, edgeB = at rate 1500). Empty array means no
  policy flips occurred anywhere in the chart between these two rates for
  that pack (true for 5 of the 6 packs here — only `frcp-civil-procedure`
  has a flip).

## Known per-pack result: `frcp-civil-procedure` absorbing-chain failure

`frcp-civil-procedure.json`'s `absorbingChain500` is `{ ok: false, error: "..." }`
— the default value-iteration policy induces a closed non-absorbing cycle
(a self-loop or mutual loop the applicant's optimal policy never escapes at
rate 500), which makes `(I − Q)` singular. This is a real, reproducible
property of that pack's content + the default policy at rate 500, not a
dump-script bug — verify parity by checking the Rust port throws/reports
the equivalent condition for the same pack, not by expecting numeric
output here.

## Generation run (for context, not itself load-bearing)

All 6 packs succeeded end-to-end; total wall time ~29s dominated by
`frcp-civil-procedure`'s Pareto enumeration (~19s across its 12 terminals,
worst single terminal ~6.9s — still under the 20s slow-path threshold, so
no terminal anywhere used the capped 20000-maxPaths override).
